acceptance_signals: The landing page keeps its current Hero, four-section main journey, CTAs, report preview, and visual structure; only the first workflow step is clarified as setting boundaries with equally compact supported wording.
Both Quickstart languages open with concise goal-oriented entry points for adopting an existing repository, starting a new repository, generating a report, and inspecting development features.
Stable install, inspect or preview, adopt or initialize, check, report, human-review boundary, and continue-reading paths appear before any detailed development material.

The existing long automatic-product, Adapter-version, MCP, and replay-safety prose no longer interrupts the stable onboarding path and remains reachable through accurate existing deep links rather than being deleted as provenance.

The development preview is one compact, clearly separated notice that distinguishes stable 0.2.1, published 0.3.0rc1, development source, installed state, and unproven state without presenting a development capability as stable.

One or at most two short expected-output examples use output captured from real current supported commands; dry-run output uses PLAN rather than invented CREATE action lines and explicitly states that no repository files were changed.
The one-command update material is secondary to the stable first-adoption journey rather than interrupting it.
Passing checks remain visibly non-authoritative for merge, release, publication, or deployment, and unrelated repository instructions or files are not described as silently overwritten.
English and Chinese pages remain semantically aligned, all internal links resolve, accessibility basics remain present, and no unrendered template or encoding regression is introduced.
The Quickstart main prose is materially shorter than the current approximately 1662-word English surface without replacing development prose with a terminal wall.

Relevant site and documentation tests, the complete suite, repository and task governance, scope reconciliation, git diff validation, and phone and desktop browser acceptance complete with unresolved gaps reported.
README current entry, STATUS current reality, and the dated development log are updated only where the user journey or closeout state requires it.
Paused task p0-quickstart-ia-cleanup-v1 remains unchanged as evidence of the corrected fail-closed path.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-334e80c206624ea79248e422652a488a and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control. Pre-implementation source-of-truth inspection found that the admitted scope omitted docs/quickstart.zh-CN.md and tests/test_interview_documentation.py, which currently require replay development commands on every Quickstart surface. The accepted information-architecture change must update that user guide and replace the old test with deep-link provenance assertions rather than hiding the commands. No page, README, test, status, log, Git, publication, release, deployment, PR, Sites-hosting, or user-configuration change was made under this task. The task is paused fail-closed and a separately reviewed replacement is required.

requirement.summary: Replace paused task p0-quickstart-ia-cleanup-v1 only because it named a nonexistent freshness-test path. Preserve the current low-density landing-page structure while changing only its first workflow label from recording a request to setting boundaries. Reorganize the English and Chinese Quickstart pages around stable user goals, exact commands, and short expected results; move development roadmap, Adapter history, and replay-safety detail out of the primary onboarding path into one concise development-preview disclosure with accurate deep links. Use real supported command output and preserve every provenance and human-authority boundary.

items: Moving development detail could accidentally delete provenance or make maturity boundaries harder to find.
A goal-oriented command chain could combine commands whose stable availability or syntax differs.
Dry-run output could be copied from the wrong repository state or imply that planned files were created.
English and Chinese Quickstart pages could drift semantically.
The previous dense homepage could be reintroduced through proof blocks or engineering badges.
Existing uncommitted publication-closeout records, the paused v1 task, and user-owned .codex configuration must remain preserved and outside new Git authority.
